---
title: "Read a CSV file into a typed table"
---

This example reads a small CSV file into a `DataFrame`, with each column's
type guessed from its values and one type declared.

It needs phibble, installed as described in
[Installation](../getting-started.qmd#installation).

The data is [`readings.csv`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/phpstats/phibble/main/docs/data/readings.csv),
six weather readings from two stations:

```text
date,station,temp_c,rain_mm,wind_kmh,windy
2024-03-01,north,7.5,0.0,12,FALSE
2024-03-01,south,9.1,1.2,31,TRUE
2024-03-02,north,6.8,NA,18,FALSE
2024-03-02,south,8.4,3.5,35,TRUE
2024-03-03,north,10.2,0.0,9,FALSE
2024-03-03,south,11.0,0.4,22,FALSE
```

Save it next to this script and run the script with `php`:

{{< include _read-a-csv.md >}}

`DataFrame::fromCsv()` guesses a type for each column, as readr's
`read_csv()` does. `date` holds ISO 8601 dates, so it is a date column.
`temp_c` and `rain_mm` hold decimals, so they are floats, and `wind_kmh` holds
whole numbers, so it is an int. `windy` holds `TRUE` and `FALSE`, so it is a
bool. The `NA` in `rain_mm` is a missing value, which phibble stores as
`null`. `types` declares `station` a factor, which the guess would have read
as a string. The type of each column prints under its name.

[Reading and writing data](../io.qmd) lists the other options of
`fromCsv()`, and [Types](../types.qmd) describes the column types.
